summary: Anthony Lake lookout on The Lakes: first cabin 1912 or 1915, cupola 1926, gone by 1966; a public summit trail today.

facts.status_note: Gone by 1966; the summit is a public hike and no source describes lookout remains.

access.note: Summit trailhead reached by a spur road off the Anthony Lake Highway, per the Oregon Hikers field guide.

visit.trail_note: About six miles round trip from Anthony Lake; a much rougher road starts only 700 feet below the summit.

events.note: First 12x12 cabin with roof platform (register, firelookout.com); a June 1915 newspaper note and the field guide say 1915
Accidentally burned in the off-season between 1924 and 1925 (firelookout.com only)
Cupola cabin replaced the first cabin (register, firelookout.com); the history site says a cupola was added to the house
Forestry student arrived in June to spend the summer at the Anthony Lakes lookout station (June 26, 1941 note)
Leo Mosher in an August 1962 newspaper note; firelookout.com lists Leo Poe
Gone by 1966; the field guide says demolished

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the first cabin to 1912. A June 1915 newspaper note and the field guide date the lookout to 1915. The story gives both.
The register and firelookout.com say a cupola cabin replaced the first cabin; the history site says an enclosed cupola was added to the house.
firelookout.com lists Leo Poe for 1962; the August 1962 newspaper note names Leo Mosher.

sources.title: Lakes Mtn. (The Lakes) Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Identity assumed: the register's Lakes Mountain site (44.94365, -118.24278, 8,522 ft) is the field guide's The Lakes Lookout above Anthony Lake. Dates and location match, but please confirm. A search snippet listed the Anthony Lakes to The Lakes Lookout trail as CLOSED on AllTrails; I did not open that page, so the story makes no closure claim. The 1962 staff name conflicts (Poe vs Mosher). Staff names come from transcriptions on the history site.
